title: Brookfield plans for a $27 billion AI data center at UK power station
description: Brookfield is targeting a massive artificial intelligence data center in the north of England, as Europe scrambles to develop infrastructure to suppor
body: Brookfield is targeting a massive artificial intelligence data center in the north of England, as Europe scrambles to develop infrastructure to support the rollout of AI amid high energy and land costs. Energy company Drax Group said Tuesday it has signed an agreement with Brookfield and the asset manager's neocloud platform Radiant to jointly develop an AI data center on the Drax Power Station estate in North Yorkshire. London-listed shares of Drax were up 8.8% in early morning trading.The project is initially targeting up to 100 megawatts of capacity to be operational from the first quarter of 2028, with an additional 500 MW of capacity to be brought online between 2028 and 2031. It is then looking to secure more than 1 gigawatt of capacity at the site by an unspecified date. Brookfield estimates total investment, including semiconductors, could exceed £20 billion ($26.8 billion), with an initial £2.5 billion investment in phase 1."This is a unique opportunity for the UK's AI ecosystem to build at scale," Radiant CEO Mahdi Yahya said in a statement. "By designing, building and operating from the UK, it will give British researchers, startups and enterprises access to frontier compute at home."The first phase of Brookfield's project in North Yorkshire will use power from the grid and target commercial customers from early 2028. The initial phase is subject to planning, regulatory and network approvals from the government and relevant agencies, alongside securing a tenant for the project, Drax said in a statement said. The company added that final investment decisions are yet to be made.Europe's AI data center pushWhile the U.S. has surged ahead on developing the huge data centers needed to power AI, Europe has been slower to break ground on the facilities. The U.K. in particular has struggled with high energy costs and challenges with long waiting times for businesses to connect to the grid.In October, it was reported that Microsoft had pulled out of a deal to anchor an Nscale data center just outside London, amid delays connecting to the country's power grid. An Nscale spokesperson told CNBC at the time that it remained "committed" to the project and was "exploring alternative power sources for the site."Unlike the U.K., the Nordics benefit from abundant power and available land. Countries in the region, like Finland, have seen major commitments to develop AI data centers this year. In September, Google said it would invest at least 13 billion euros ($15.1 billion) into AI infrastructure in the country, marking the tech giant's largest single investment in Europe.

schema.headline: Brookfield plans for a $27 billion AI data center at UK power station

title: Aramco's profit rises as refining margins strengthen amid Iran war
description: The Saudi Aramco logo is pictured at Hyvolution exhibition in Paris, France, February 1, 2024. Benoit Tessier | ReutersAramco reported a 9% rise in th
body: The Saudi Aramco logo is pictured at Hyvolution exhibition in Paris, France, February 1, 2024. Benoit Tessier | ReutersAramco reported a 9% rise in third-quarter adjusted net income on Tuesday on stronger refining margins.The Saudi oil giant posted adjusted net income of $31.2 billion for the quarter, up from $28.6 billion a year earlier. The figure exceeded the median analyst consensus estimate of $30.66 billion, according to the company.Aramco's downstream business, which processes crude oil into fuels and other products, posted adjusted earnings before interest and taxes of $10.3 billion, up 234% from a year earlier, driven by stronger refining margins."Geopolitical uncertainty and attacks on key energy facilities continued to amplify the global energy supply crisis in the third quarter of 2026, with serious implications for global energy security," Aramco CEO Amin H. Nasser said in a statement.Nasser said the company's operational flexibility and supply network enabled it to continue delivering energy to customers despite the disruptions. Aramco is also exploring additional overseas storage capacity and alternative export routes to strengthen its global supply network.The company generated $28.2 billion in free cash flow during the quarter, up from $23.6 billion a year earlier.Aramco said its board declared a third-quarter base dividend of $21.9 billion, up 3.5% year on year, to be paid in the fourth quarter.The company also said its major upstream projects remained on track and highlighted its acquisition of a 49% stake in Saudi artificial intelligence company HUMAIN.– CNBC's Emma Graham contributed to this story.

schema.headline: Aramco's profit rises as refining margins strengthen amid Iran war

title: Yum Brands earnings beat estimates, but cyclospora outbreak weighs on Taco Bell
description: A woman leaving Taco Bell on July 28, 2026, in Washington,DC. The Washington Post | Getty ImagesYum Brands on Tuesday reported earnings that beat expe
body: A woman leaving Taco Bell on July 28, 2026, in Washington,DC. The Washington Post | Getty ImagesYum Brands on Tuesday reported earnings that beat expectations, but a cyclospora outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce at Taco Bell weighed on the company's same-store sales growth.However, Yum said Taco Bell, which the company considers a "growth engine" for its business, has since rebounded. "Since the end of September, Taco Bell U.S. has been outpacing the [quick-service restaurant] industry on same-store sales growth," Yum CEO Chris Turner said in a statement.Taco Bell's same-store sales are up about 1% so far in the fourth quarter, CFO Ranjith Roy said on the company's earnings conference call Tuesday. In the last four weeks ended Friday, same-store sales have risen 3% compared with the year-ago period.Here's what the company reported compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:Earnings per share: $1.56 adjusted vs. $1.49 expectedRevenue: $2.05 billion vs. $2.05 billion expectedYum reported fiscal third-quarter net income of $1.62 billion, or $5.92 per share, up from $397 million, or $1.41 per share, a year earlier.Excluding gains from its divestiture of Pizza Hut and other items, the restaurant company earned $1.56 per share.Net sales rose 4% to $2.05 billion.During the quarter, Yum completed its divestiture of Pizza Hut. It closed the sale of the pizza chain's business in mainland China to Yum China on Aug. 7 and sold the rest of Pizza Hut to LongRange Capital on Sept. 1. The company's third-quarter results include Pizza Hut up until those dates.Excluding Pizza Hut, Yum's same-store sales were flat for the quarter as Taco Bell weighed on the company's overall results. Taco Bell's same-store sales declined by 4% as diners temporarily pulled back on visits due to the foodborne illness outbreak.Yum executives previously said the weekend of July 18 saw the most severe impact to sales, but trends have improved since then. Taco Bell's most loyal customers returned faster, Yum said, thanks in part to weekly Tuesday deals for loyalty program members after the cyclospora outbreak took over headlines. Traffic from "medium" and "light" customers has bounced back to about 95% of prior levels, while visits from "heavy" users is back to normal, Roy said. To attract more casual diners, Taco Bell has been relying on star power, like a collaboration with pop star Olivia Rodrigo on a pink-colored Mountain Dew Baja Blast.Outside of the U.S., Taco Bell's much smaller international business reported same-store sales growth of 5%.KFC's same-store sales ticked up 1%, helped by system sales growth in China and Europe. The U.S., now the chicken chain's third-largest market, saw system sales shrink 6% in the quarter. Like Restaurant Brands International's Popeyes, KFC has struggled in the U.S. amid a wave of new competitors and more budget-conscious consumers. Its home market represents only about 5% of KFC's operating profit, but it remains a symbolically important part of the business for Yum investors. During the quarter, KFC U.S. launched popcorn chicken, which sold out in many restaurants. However, Yum said the limited-time menu item was not enough to offset the successful Hot & Spicy Wings and Potato Wedges promotion during the year-ago period.Globally, KFC is trying to become "the most modern chicken QSR," Turner said on the company's earnings conference call. To achieve that lofty goal, he said the chain will roll out buzzy promotions, a new brand identity, and a wider menu that includes upgraded sauces and more beverages.

schema.headline: Yum Brands earnings beat estimates, but cyclospora outbreak weighs on Taco Bell

title: Australia hikes rates to 18-year high to fight inflation
description: Michele Bullock, governor of the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), during a news conference at the central bank's head office in Sydney, Australia, on
body: Michele Bullock, governor of the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), during a news conference at the central bank's head office in Sydney, Australia, on Tuesday, May 5, 2026. Australia's central bank raised its key interest rate for a third consecutive meeting, underscoring its determination to tame stubbornly strong inflation and cementing its outlier status among global counterparts. Photographer: Brendon Thorne/Bloomberg via Getty ImagesBloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesAustralia's central bank raised its benchmark cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85% on Tuesday, the highest level since November 2008.The Reserve Bank of Australia's move was in line with expectations from economists polled by Reuters, and marked its fifth rate increase this year.In its statement, the RBA said that the move was a split decision, with six members voting for the increase and three opting for a hold. This also comes as the country continues to grapple with high inflation, with the consumer price index rising 4.3% in September, up from 4% in August and marking its highest level since March.The central bank also said inflation is now expected to "remain elevated through much of 2027," and not expected to fall back into its 2%-3% target range till late 2027, three quarters later than previously forecast. This was due to higher fuel and other commodity prices, in addition to factors including AI-related investment, which is driving rapid growth in prices for technology-related goods, the RBA said.In its September decision, RBA governor Michelle Bullock said that inflation is "too high," driven by higher oil prices from the Iran War and stronger domestic spending. "We're seeing signs that upside risks to inflation are materializing," she added, saying that additional hikes will come "if that's what's needed to get inflation down."Growth has slowed in the first two quarters of 2026. Australia's GDP rose 2.1% in the June quarter compared to a year earlier, down from 2.5% in the March quarter.The RBA is trying to bring inflation back under control while higher borrowing costs and cost-of-living pressures weigh on households and activity. When asked if she sees a recession for Australia, Bullock said that it is "not our base case at the moment."

schema.headline: Australia hikes rates to 18-year high to fight inflation

title: Shopify falls 9% after Q3 revenue and merchandise volume miss estimates
description: Dado Ruvic | ReutersShares of e-commerce platform Shopify plunged 9% in early trading on Tuesday after the company missed estimates on subscription gr
body: Dado Ruvic | ReutersShares of e-commerce platform Shopify plunged 9% in early trading on Tuesday after the company missed estimates on subscription gross profit and gross merchandise volume.Shopify reported before the bell Tuesday and posted adjusted earnings of 49 cents per share, topping LSEG estimates of 46 cents per share. Overall, quarterly revenue of $3.74 billion came in just below LSEG estimates of $3.75 billion. Shopify said it sees revenue growth in the "low thirties" range year over year for the fourth quarter, versus LSEG estimates of 32.1%.Gross merchandise volume, which came in at $119.15 billion, missed analyst estimates of $120.03 billion for the quarter, according to StreetAccount. Subscription gross profit also missed estimates by nearly $20 million, coming in at $661 million compared to StreetAccount estimates of $680.3 million. Merchant gross profit beat estimates.Subscription revenue of $836 million also missed analyst estimates of $848.1 million, according to FactSet. title: Bill Ackman warns of 'casino' stock market as speculative trading grows
description: Pershing Square CEO Bill Ackman speaking on CNBC's Squawk Box on Nov. 3rd, 2026.CNBCBill Ackman worries that the stock market is broken, saying the ri
body: Pershing Square CEO Bill Ackman speaking on CNBC's Squawk Box on Nov. 3rd, 2026.CNBCBill Ackman worries that the stock market is broken, saying the rise of speculative trading is leading to wild price swings thanks to the amount of leverage in the system."Every number of days, I feel like markets are broken," Ackman told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Tuesday. "Stocks trade at prices that make no sense to me. Yes, it's good if you're a long-term investor and you can buy at a stupid price. I don't think it's good for the country generally.""We're back to the casino type markets when there was 95% leverage," he added. "I don't think that's inherently good for the economy, for society, and it's leading to these massive moves in stocks."The founder of Pershing Square Capital Management said those same dislocations in the market have given the hedge fund the opportunity to snag big bargains.watch nowPershing bought Microsoft, for example, when it was pummeled during the "SaaSpocalypse" earlier this year, and Amazon when it fell following President Donald Trump's tariffs. It also bought Alphabet when the stock moved "massively" following ChatGPT's launch, he said.But the billionaire investor worries that the rise of one-day leveraged vehicles, perpetual futures and sports betting is dangerous for investors who are treating the stock market as a get-rich-quick scheme — an attitude that could have disastrous consequences."It's good for us long term, us being Pershing Square," he said. "I don't think it's good for the country."Among the stocks Ackman is especially bullish on are Visa and Mastercard, which he called among the world's "greatest" businesses, as well as streaming platform Netflix, in which he disclosed a position in August.

schema.headline: Bill Ackman warns of 'casino' stock market as speculative trading grows

title: A little-known biotech’s high-stakes cancer bet just paid off and its shares doubled
description: Danish biotech Genmab has seen its shares double in three months after a string of major cancer drug trial successes, giving fresh momentum to its pus
body: Danish biotech Genmab has seen its shares double in three months after a string of major cancer drug trial successes, giving fresh momentum to its push to take greater control of the medicines it develops and sells.Shares in the roughly $35 billion company surged 48% last week, including a 29% jump in a single session after strong results for petosemtamab, its experimental head and neck cancer treatment. The announcement marked Genmab's third successful Phase 3 trial in October, following positive results for treatments targeting ovarian cancer and lymphoma.After nearly three decades spent building Genmab into one of Europe's prominent biotechnology companies, CEO Jan van de Winkel told CNBC on Friday the breakthroughs marked "a completely new era."Historically, Genmab made money from royalties from drugs it helped develop, including Johnson & Johnson's multiple myeloma treatment Darzalex and Novartis' Kesimpta. Van de Winkel said Johnson & Johnson is expected to generate $16.5 billion to $16.9 billion in Darzalex sales this year, with Genmab receiving royalties of up to 20%. Genmab is now using that financial firepower to build a business that keeps a much larger share of the revenue from its own treatments.Cancer breakthroughsThe biggest market reaction followed Genmab's Oct. 28 announcement that petosemtamab, combined with Merck's Keytruda, reduced the risk of death by 50% compared with Keytruda alone in a Phase 3 trial of patients with recurrent or metastatic head and neck cancer.The combination also significantly improved response rates and showed no new safety signals, according to Genmab.Van de Winkel told CNBC the combination "could potentially set a completely new standard" of care although he declined to say whether the survival data might hold up as the data mature, citing still unpublished full data.Days earlier, Genmab reported that its medicine Rina-S reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 71% and the risk of death by 57% versus chemotherapy in a Phase 3 ovarian cancer trial. Barclays analysts said the results exceeded investor expectations and suggested Rina-S could offer an alternative for patients ineligible for AbbVie's competing treatment Elahere, or whose cancer had progressed after receiving it. They cautioned, however, that cross-trial comparisons are limited.Stock Chart IconStock chart iconGenmab shares have nearly doubled over the past three months. A third late-stage October win came from Epkinly, co-developed with AbbVie, which reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 51% when combined with standard chemotherapy in previously untreated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.Analysts see significant commercial potential for petosemtamab, including beyond its initial target market. Jefferies analysts said the drug could generate $3.5 billion in peak annual global sales treating recurrent or metastatic head and neck cancer, and estimated an expansion into locally advanced disease could add another $3.5 billion, an opportunity they believe investors have yet to fully appreciate. Declining to give specific numbers, van de Winkel said he expects petosemtamab to become a "multi-billion dollar drug."Genmab is due to report third-quarter earnings on Nov. 5.Antibody specialist Genmab has built its business around antibody-based medicines, including so-called bispecific antibodies such as petosemtamab, which can bind to two different targets on cancer cells simultaneously.Petosemtamab targets the proteins EGFR and LGR5, and is designed to both disrupt signals that help cancer cells grow and to encourage the immune system to attack the tumor.Van de Winkel said Genmab's expertise in antibodies and their interaction with the immune system has also helped it spot promising medicines developed by others. It acquired petosemtamab through an $8 billion purchase of Merus in 2025 and Rina-S through a $1.8 billion acquisition of ProfoundBio in 2024. Those deals are also central to Genmab's changing business model.It fully owns petosemtamab and Rina-S, while splitting the commercial economics of Epkinly equally with AbbVie, much larger shares than with Johnson & Johnson and Novartis."From now on I'm going to increasingly hold on to ownership of these new medicines," Van de Winkel said. Genmab now has 15 Phase 3 trials across its three lead compounds."The model is beginning to be validated and click together," he said. "I think the market gets it at this point finally."The Merus deal underscored the scale of the bet. Genmab borrowed $5.5 billion to help fund the purchase, relying on its royalty income as a financial backstop if petosemtamab failed.A new chapterOwning more of its medicines also means taking on more of the work of selling them. Van de Winkel said the company already has much of the necessary infrastructure in place, having built up commercial capabilities around existing treatments including Epkinly and Tivdak, co-developed with Pfizer. The company is expanding its sales presence in Europe and seeking to reach more cancer patients through community healthcare, beyond specialist hospitals, in the U.S.Van de Winkel said he wants Genmab's majority-owned medicines to reach around 500,000 patients by the 2030s, up from fewer than 30,000 today.Westend61 | Westend61 | Getty ImagesHe also acknowledged potential interest from larger drugmakers, saying Genmab was likely "high up on the radar screen," but stressed that his ambition remained to build an independent European biotech.Greater ownership, however, also means bearing more of the cost and risk of clinical trials, regulatory approvals and commercialization.Van de Winkel acknowledged that geopolitical shifts and drug-pricing pressures could complicate expansion plans and change the order in which Genmab launches medicines in different markets.

schema.headline: A little-known biotech’s high-stakes cancer bet just paid off and its shares doubled

title: Trump is going to get 'trounced' in the midterms — and knows it, Anthony Scaramucci tells CNBC
description: watch nowU.S. President Donald Trump will get "trounced" in Tuesday's midterm elections, former White House communications director and SkyBridge Capi
body: watch nowU.S. President Donald Trump will get "trounced" in Tuesday's midterm elections, former White House communications director and SkyBridge Capital founder Anthony Scaramucci told CNBC.Speaking to CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Tuesday, Scaramucci said America is in the throes of a cultural and economic struggle, with the two main parties fighting to deliver "two different visions of where the country should go.""I think the president's going to get trounced, by the way, and I think he knows he's going to get trounced," he said.Trump's economic approval rating hit an all-time low last month, according to CNBC's All-America Economic Survey, with 65% of respondents disapproving of the president's handling of the economy, while 80% rated the economy as fair or poor."You have one vote. You have one customer relations survey that you can do on the American president — that's at the midterms, and people are not happy," Scaramucci added."He promised affordability, he promised no more forever wars, he promised transparency on the Epstein files," Scaramucci said on Tuesday. "He didn't deliver on any of that stuff, and so there's a lot of people inside MAGA that are now also breaking from him."The White House did not immediately respond to a CNBC request to comment. The White House previously told CNBC that Scaramucci's "relevance ended almost a decade ago." Scaramucci was White House communications director for 10 days in 2017, during Trump's first term.  Prediction markets are now pricing in around a three-in-four chance of the Democrats winning control of the Senate in Tuesday's election. Odds and gambling platforms do not use methodologies used by traditional political polling, and therefore are not substitutes for political polls.Scaramucci 'bearish' on Iran breakthroughOn the Iran war, Scaramucci said he was "bearish" on a potential diplomatic breakthrough after the ballot. "I don't see any alignment between the Iranians, the Israelis, and the Americans for a potential negotiated solution right now," he said. "If the Americans are going to ramp up the military strikes alongside of the Israelis ... I don't really understand how that's going to necessarily help the region either."The U.S. launched "defensive" strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island overnight, a U.S. official told MS Now. Trump previously said American forces would not attack Iran before the midterms."Wars are very bad for business," Scaramucci told CNBC Tuesday. "They're not great for the stock market. So I would like to have a negotiated settlement, but there's nothing on the matrix where you see the concentric circles lining up, where these three groups would say, 'okay, that's a deal that all three of us are willing to accept.'"Republican 'civil war'Scaramucci also said "disarray" within the Democratic Party had been "the best thing that has happened for Donald Trump.""And so, if he gets trounced here, there will be bicameral investigations that will be the main show because there's a lot of things that's going on in the administration that the Democrats are going to want to uncover," he said. "The Republicans, in my mind, I think there'll be a great intellectual civil war. The Republicans are going to have to reconcile where do they want to go. It's no longer the party of Ronald Reagan, certainly not the party of George W. Bush, but is it the party of Donald Trump after he leaves the stage?"Scaramucci added that it was going to take a long while to get away from the so-called MAGA movement. "There'll be DNA elements of MAGA in the next presidential candidate for sure, because looming large over that presidential candidate will be Donald Trump and several hundred million dollars of his PAC money, and so they're not going to want to get too far away from him in 2028. So there will be elements of MAGA, but I also think there'll be a civil war in that party," he said.

schema.headline: Trump is going to get 'trounced' in the midterms — and knows it, Anthony Scaramucci tells CNBC

title: Russia confirms new Ukraine peace talks as Melania Trump prepares to host ceasefire meeting
description: US First Lady Melania Trump during the Presidential AI Challenge National Champion awards ceremony in the East Room of the White House in Washington,
body: US First Lady Melania Trump during the Presidential AI Challenge National Champion awards ceremony in the East Room of the White House in Washington, DC, US, on Tuesday, June 9, 2026. Daniel Heuer | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesRussia on Tuesday confirmed that peace talks with Ukraine and the U.S. will go ahead next week in Abu Dhabi, while also signaling that a meeting between Presidents Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to end the conflict was on the table. Putin aide Vladimir ​Medinsky will serve ⁠as Moscow's chief negotiator ​at the talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11, Kremlin spokesman ​Dmitry Peskov told reporters on a conference call, according to Reuters. Separately, First Lady Melania Trump will bring Russian and Ukrainian representatives to the White House to discuss the local ceasefire in Kherson, the White House said Tuesday.Monday saw the end of a six-day ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky and surrounding areas in the Kherson region to allow for evacuation of residents, in a pause of hostilities that the White House said was brokered by the first lady.KHERSON, UKRAINE - OCTOBER 28: During a ceasefire, a man on a bicycle rides past residential buildings previously damaged by Russian strikes on October 28, 2026 in Kherson, Ukraine. (Photo by Ivan Antypenko/Suspilne Ukraine/JSC "UA:PBC"/Global Images Ukraine via Getty Images)Global Images Ukraine | Global Images Ukraine | Getty ImagesUkraine on Monday accused Russia of using the ceasefire to reinforce its military positions in the city.The first lady's summit on Thursday will be "an extraordinary moment in American history," the White House said, but did not name the representatives who will attend. Melania Trump will deliver remarks on the Oleshky ceasefire at 11 a.m. ET Thursday, it added.Peskov also said Tuesday the Kremlin hopes to finalize plans for a trilateral meeting between the leaders of Russia, the U.S., and China in the coming days. The comments follow earlier reports that these countries were planning to negotiate an end to the war in Ukraine, without Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at the table.Zelenskyy has said that any negotiations over Ukraine's future must include Kyiv. "It can be acceptable only when we are at the table of negotiations," he said on Oct. 20, adding that he had discussed the proposal of a three-way meeting between the U.S., China, and Russia to negotiate an end to the nearly five-year full-scale war. "Nothing about Ukraine without Ukraine," he said.Read more of CNBC's Russia-Ukraine coverage:Fake nuclear warnings in Ukraine as Moscow, Kyiv report separate cyberattacks on emergency appsRussian strikes plunge Ukrainian city into blackout as Zelenskyy warns of more missile attacksTrump's Russia diesel deal may offer Putin more than money — and spell trouble for UkraineZelenskyy accuses Russia of violating Trump’s energy ceasefire as drone attacks continueTrump declares ‘energy ceasefire’ between Russia and Ukraine; Zelenskyy is waiting for detailsUkraine’s surprise robot offensive exposes a vulnerability in Putin’s war machinePutin orders army expansion as Zelenskyy warns Russia preparing to deploy 10,000 North Korean troopsRussia ‘truly’ appreciates U.S. invite to G20 summit — but hasn’t decided if Putin will goZelenskyy says Ukraine ready for ‘energy ceasefire,’ calls for trilateral meeting with Putin, TrumpPutin floats ‘chance’ at peace with Ukraine as NATO chief warns Russia is becoming ‘increasingly reckless’Russia preparing ‘massive strikes’ on Ukraine’s energy sites after deadliest attack of the yearRussia's economy has defied the skeptics. Cracks are getting harder to hide'Winter is coming’: Ukraine fears its toughest test since Russia’s full-scale invasionTensions between the U.S. and Ukraine have mounted over recent weeks amid continued strikes between Moscow and Kyiv, including on civilian and energy targets. A series of moves by the Trump administration in October raised questions about Washington's reliability as Kyiv's most important military partner. Tuesday's announcement follows U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff saying late Monday that Washington will mediate Ukraine-Russia peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11, focusing on security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian issues. Witkoff also said that U.S. negotiators will meet European and NATO officials in Brussels this week to discuss post-war security guarantees and Ukraine's reconstruction.

schema.headline: Russia confirms new Ukraine peace talks as Melania Trump prepares to host ceasefire meeting

title: Ferrari raises 2026 guidance after Q3 earnings beat
description: Workers on the production line at the new Ferrari NV E-building factory in Maranello, Italy, on Friday, June 21, 2024. Francesca Volpi | Bloomberg | G
body: Workers on the production line at the new Ferrari NV E-building factory in Maranello, Italy, on Friday, June 21, 2024. Francesca Volpi | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesFerrari on Tuesday raised its 2026 guidance after the sports car maker slightly beat Wall Street's third-quarter expectations.Here's how Ferrari performed in the third quarter compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG:Earnings per share: 2.44 euros ($2.77) adjusted vs. 2.37 euros expectedRevenue: 1.9 billion euros vs. 1.89 billion euros expectedFerrari raised its guidance to revenue of 7.65 billion euros, up from 7.6 billion euros; adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization to 3 billion euros, up from 2.97 billion euros; and adjusted EPS to at least 9.85 euros, up from at least 9.68 euros.The automaker also upgraded its expectations for industrial free cash flow to up to 1.65 billion euros, up from previous expectations for at least 1.55 billion euros.This is the second consecutive quarter Ferrari has raised its 2026 guidance, despite vehicle shipments being lower by 318 units through the first nine months of the year, at 10,170 vehicles, compared with last year. The decline is led by fewer shipments to the Americas and China, Hong Kong and Taiwan.Ferrari said Tuesday that the guidance improvements were a result of stronger-than-expected customer personalizations, lower than anticipated currency headwinds and a second place finish in the Formula 1 championship."Our order book now reaches into 2028, and we still have two more launches to come this year. In addition, we continue to create engaging events around the world to further tighten the bonds with our clients and partners across Racing, Sports Cars and Lifestyle," Ferrari CEO Benedetto Vigna said in a release.RBC Capital Markets analyst Tom Narayan said Tuesday that Ferrari's results were largely in line with Wall Street expectations. However, he said shares may be under "under slight pressure given some were hoping for a bigger guidance raise, but expect it to get better once folks realize these results are healthy."Ferrari's U.S. shares initially declined on the results before turning positive and were up roughly  2% during premarket trading.

schema.headline: Ferrari raises 2026 guidance after Q3 earnings beat

title: Blackstone president calls for more equity to fund AI buildout as debt risks mount
description: Jon Gray, president and chief operating officer of Blackstone Inc., during the Global Financial Leaders' Investment Summit in Hong Kong, China, on Tue
body: Jon Gray, president and chief operating officer of Blackstone Inc., during the Global Financial Leaders' Investment Summit in Hong Kong, China, on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. This year's event brings together around 280 global financial leaders, including roughly 120 group chairs and CEOs, with the outlook for markets, the global economy and rapid advances in technology among the big themes. Photographer: Anthony Kwan/Bloomberg via Getty ImagesBloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesThe artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout will need more equity financing as lenders become increasingly exposed to the companies driving the buildout, Blackstone President Jon Gray said Tuesday.Speaking at the Hong Kong Monetary Authority’s Global Financial Leaders’ Investment Summit, Gray said the scale of capital required for AI is creating concentration risks for debt investors, both across the sector and at individual companies.Unlike shareholders, who can benefit from a company's growth, lenders have limited upside as their returns are largely confined to interest and principal repayments, he said.There’s going to be more equity needed across this space to keep up with these enormous demands.Jon GrayPresident & COO, Blackstone Inc.Speaking at the same panel, Pimco CEO Emmanuel Roman warned investors that the scale of AI financing could prove to be "too much" for markets to absorb.Roman said AI-related capital spending could reach around $10 trillion over the next five years, citing General Atlantic CEO Bill Ford's estimate. He added that about $550 billion in AI debt had been issued in various forms so far this year.Even with a mix of equity and debt financing, the amount required would be “gigantic,” Roman said, comparing it with a global corporate bond market of roughly $20 trillion.“At some point in time, it’s going to be too much,” he said. Global data center demand will require about $8.5 trillion in capital spending over the next five years, Goldman Sachs wrote in a report Monday.Gray said financing the buildout would require a combination of public markets, banks and private capital, with companies increasingly turning to structured transactions to limit the amount of debt they take on. Cash generated by hyperscalers would also fund part of the spending, he said.“The creativity is needed because the scale of capital is enormous," Gray said. Despite those financing challenges, Gray remained bullish on AI infrastructure, saying demand for computing power was “running well ahead of supply.”Spending on AI models across Blackstone’s portfolio companies had risen 20-fold over the past year as businesses saw financial benefits from uses including coding, customer engagement and content creation, he said.Meeting that demand remains difficult, however, as securing sites, permits, chips, power and capital becomes more challenging, according to Gray.

title: Versant earnings beat expectations as digital platforms drive growth
description: Versant Media celebrates its initial public offering at the Nasdaq, Jan. 5, 2026.Versant MediaVersant Media on Tuesday reported quarterly earnings and
body: Versant Media celebrates its initial public offering at the Nasdaq, Jan. 5, 2026.Versant MediaVersant Media on Tuesday reported quarterly earnings and revenue that beat expectations and reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance, citing strength across its portfolio and growth in its platforms revenue.The media company reported $245 million in revenue from digital platforms including Fandango, marking a nearly 10% year-over-year increase. Versant said Fandango saw "significant growth" in ticketing revenue in the third quarter, notching its highest level since the pandemic. Advertising revenue, however, slipped to $373 million during the period, down 5.3% from last year, primarily due to the impact of last year's Ryder Cup, according to the company. The Versant portfolio includes CNBC, MS NOW, Golf Channel and other cable and digital properties. Here's how the company performed in its third quarter, compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:Earnings per share: 34 cents vs. 5 cents expectedRevenue: $1.59 billion vs. $1.57 billion expectedVersant completed four major distribution renewals this year following its spinoff from Comcast's NBCUniversal. "We understood the questions raised at the time of the spin about our ability to secure attractive carriage renewals," CEO Mark Lazarus said on a call with analysts. "We've now answered that question: 75% of our network subscribers are now under contract into 2028 and beyond, so we have clear visibility going forward."During the third quarter, Versant said, its networks reached more than 120 million viewers monthly and its aggregate viewership grew by double digits year over year. The company also launched MS NOW's direct-to-consumer product and Fandango's on-demand product as new growth drivers. CNBC is expected to launch a direct-to-consumer product next year, Versant said.For the period ended Sept. 30, Versant recorded net income of $47 million, or 34 cents per share, compared with $80 million, or 56 cents per share, the year prior. Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization was $353 million, beating Wall Street estimates of $305 million, according to StreetAccount.Revenue fell slightly to $1.59 billion from $1.66 billion in the year-ago period. The company said its revenue figure included the acquisition of golf simulation company Full Swing and the sale of sports management software company SportsEngine. The company reaffirmed its full-year revenue outlook of between $6.2 billion and $6.45 billion and its adjusted EBITDA outlook of $1.9 billion to $2.05 billion. It adjusted part of its full-year guidance, saying it now expects free cash flow to exceed the prior range of between $1 billion and $1.2 billion. "We're building on strong relationships we already have with consumers, advertisers and distributors," Lazarus said on the call. "We're finding new ways to reach and serve those audiences. We have the brands, the financial strength and the people to execute this transition successfully."Versant began trading as a standalone company on the Nasdaq in January after separating from Comcast. Though it began largely as a portfolio of cable networks, Versant executives have said they intend to diversify the company's revenue mix to eventually draw 50% from digital, platform, subscription, ad-supported and transactional businesses. During the third quarter, revenue from linear TV decreased 5.8% to $935 million as the segment sees pressure from cord-cutting and subscriber declines. Live sports continues to be a major driver for the company. Versant said it saw "robust audience engagement" in the third quarter and that WNBA viewership on Versant's USA Sports networks was 25% higher than the prior year's cable average.Versant also announced an additional $100 million accelerated stock repurchase program beginning Wednesday. It expects that transaction to be completed during the fourth quarter. Disclosure: Versant Media is the parent company of CNBC.

schema.headline: Versant earnings beat expectations as digital platforms drive growth

title: Pfizer hikes full-year outlook as newer products grow, taps company veteran as new CFO
description: Smith Collection | Archive Photos | Getty ImagesPfizer on Tuesday reported fiscal third-quarter results that topped estimates and hiked its full-year
body: Smith Collection | Archive Photos | Getty ImagesPfizer on Tuesday reported fiscal third-quarter results that topped estimates and hiked its full-year outlook, as demand for its newly launched and acquired products grows. Pfizer also Tuesday announced that Cecile Guegan, who has held various finance leadership roles at the company over the last two decades, stepped in as chief financial officer this month. She had served as interim CFO since August, when Pfizer's former CFO, Dave Denton, stepped down to take the same position at Nike.The company is now expecting full-year revenue to total $62 billion to $64 billion, which compares with a previous outlook of $60.5 billion to $62.5 billion. The low end of that sales range would be roughly flat or down slightly compared with 2025 revenue of $62.6 billion. Still, Pfizer cited its "strong year-to-date performance" as a driver for the guidance hike. The pharmaceutical giant now expects full-year adjusted profit of between $2.95 and $3.05 per share. That compares with previous guidance of between $2.80 and $3 per share. That includes a one-time $650 million charge, or a negative impact of 10 cents per share, recorded in the third quarter tied to the company's licensing and collaboration agreement with Chinese cancer drugmaker Innovent Biologics. Pfizer is working on a comeback story after its massive pandemic-era success waned. As demand for Covid products drops and generic rivals threaten its biggest moneymakers, CEO Albert Bourla is looking to jump-start growth through strategic acquisitions, fresh cancer drugs and a big bet on weight loss treatments through its acquisition of Metsera. Pfizer in August expanded its multiyear cost-cutting efforts to help offset sharp declines in Covid product sales, and is now targeting roughly $9.7 billion in net savings through 2029. Here's what the company reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: 87 cents adjusted vs. 73 cents expectedRevenue: $16.58 billion vs. $15.87 billion expectedTune in at 1:30 p.m. ET as Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla joins CNBC TV to discuss the company's earnings. Watch in real time on CNBC+ or the CNBC Pro stream.Pfizer reported third-quarter revenue of $16.58 billion, relatively flat from the same period a year ago. The company cited an operational decrease of $57 million, primarily due to lower Covid revenues, and a $15 million negative impact from foreign exchange. That was offset by strong sales of key products like its blood thinner Eliquis and targeted cancer drug Padcev, which jumped and beat expectations. Eliquis in particular raked in $2.52 billion in sales, up 25%. Analysts were expecting revenue of $2.40 billion, according to StreetAccount. Padcev posted $720 million in revenue for the period, which compares with the $658 million that analysts were expecting.Sales of Pfizer's newly launched and acquired products grew 32% operationally. That includes Padcev, its respiratory syncytial virus vaccine Abrysvo, its pneumococcal shot Prevnar 20 and oral lung cancer drug Lorbrena, among several other products. Pfizer's Covid products also topped estimates for the quarter despite seeing steep sales declines. The company's Covid vaccine generated $808 million in sales, which compares with the $770.4 million that analysts were expecting, StreetAccount estimates show. Meanwhile, Pfizer's antiviral pill, Paxlovid, booked $449 million in sales, coming in above the $394.1 million that analysts were expecting. The company booked net income of $3.24 billion, or 56 cents per share, for the period. That compares with net income of $3.54 billion, or 62 cents per share, during the third quarter of 2025. Excluding certain items, including restructuring charges and costs associated with intangible assets, Pfizer posted earnings per share of 87 cents for the quarter.

schema.headline: Pfizer hikes full-year outlook as newer products grow, taps company veteran as new CFO

title: Trump Account holders to receive SpaceX stock from Gwynne Shotwell in December
description: SpaceX President and Chief Operating Officer Gwynne Shotwell celebrates with family and other SpaceX employees at the Nasdaq Marketsite in New York af
body: SpaceX President and Chief Operating Officer Gwynne Shotwell celebrates with family and other SpaceX employees at the Nasdaq Marketsite in New York after the SpaceX initial public offering on June 12, 2026.Spencer Platt | Getty Images News | Getty ImagesEligible Trump Account holders will begin receiving donated shares of SpaceX stock next month, according to an X post on Friday."Robert and I are thrilled that our gift of over 2 million shares of SpaceX stock will be distributed to children's Trump accounts in December!" President and COO Gwynne Shotwell wrote in the post. The gift from Shotwell and her husband will provide a share apiece to around 2 million Trump Accounts holders ages 11 to 17 who live in ZIP codes with median family incomes of $57,000 or less, or in ZIP codes with too few residents for a median family income to be reported by the U.S. Census Bureau. These families should receive a notice by Monday, Shotwell wrote on X. "In a few weeks, an additional gift will be finalized for eligible 11 to 17-year-old children in military families serving overseas, children in foster care, and more children whose MFI is $90,000 or less living in counties near our home in the great state of Texas," she also wrote. Parents or guardians can check eligibility for the donation through Invest America, a nonprofit advocacy group, and track account activity with the Trump Accounts app.Read more CNBC personal finance coverageMidterm election: How affordability and the economy could affect voters' decisionsThese Senate races may help determine the fate of Social SecuritySocial Security: How much money beneficiaries may lose if Congress does nothingTrump Account holders to receive SpaceX stock from Gwynne Shotwell in DecemberCNBC's Financial Advisor 100: Best financial advisors, top firms for 2026 rankedCNBC Elite Advisors: Top ultra-high net worth wealth management firms for 2026Trump Accounts, also known as 530A accounts, are open to any U.S. child under 18 with a Social Security number.Children born from 2025 through 2028 may also receive a one-time $1,000 deposit from the U.S. Department of the Treasury. Other funds may also be available, depending on certain criteria. In a separate funding announcement in October, Elon Musk wrote in an X post that he plans to give every kid in America a share of SpaceX sometime in 2027, which may also come via Trump Accounts. The U.S. Department of the Treasury rolled out temporary regulations at the end of September that allow Trump Accounts to hold donated individual stocks, a change from previous guidelines that only allowed diversified, low-cost index funds.The move to permit stock donations could pave the way for more large-scale philanthropic gifts, Internal Revenue Service CEO Frank Bisignano told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Oct. 8. On Oct. 29, Bisignano announced his own donation to Trump Accounts for eligible children ages 2 to 8 living in 11234, Bisignano's hometown ZIP code, according to The Bisignano Family Fund.

title: Baked by Melissa enters Target with first at-home cupcake mix
description: Baked by Melissa is rolling out bite-size cupcake liners, pans and at-home baking kits in Target stores.Source: Baked by MelissaBaked by Melissa will
body: Baked by Melissa is rolling out bite-size cupcake liners, pans and at-home baking kits in Target stores.Source: Baked by MelissaBaked by Melissa will enter the at-home baking aisle in Target stores as the retailer tries to persuade shoppers to spend more at its locations this holiday season.  As of Sunday, Target is exclusively selling the brand's cupcake kits, liners and a cupcake pan, all in the dessert company's signature bite-size portions. The line includes three cupcake flavors: Christmas Tie-Dye, Marshmallow Hot Cocoa and Red Velvet. The company's entry into at-home baking comes as a number of restaurants turn to consumer packaged goods to boost sales in an otherwise challenging time for the industry. Some players, such as California Pizza Kitchen and TGI Fridays, have licensed their brands for frozen foods for decades. But other restaurant chains, including Chick-fil-A and Dutch Bros, have leaned into grocery products much more recently. For smaller companies, such as Momofuku or Carbone, space on a grocery shelf helps extend brand reach and gives consumers a chance to try their food without a reservation and at a much lower cost.   Founded by Melissa Ben-Ishay in 2008, Baked by Melissa has nine permanent locations in the New York area and ships its minicupcakes nationwide.The regional chain has garnered attention outside the city thanks to Ben-Ishay's social media presence. On TikTok, the Baked by Melissa account has more than 2.8 million followers, fueled by popular recipe videos, such as for her green goddess salad dressing. Ben-Ishay's social media stardom has led to collaborations with Ferrero and Wonder.Baked by Melissa had discussed at-home baking products for years, but Ben-Ishay, who is also president of the company, only decided to take the plunge a year ago during a trip to Target with her two kids, she told CNBC. A spin through the baking aisle made her decide Baked by Melissa "should be here," she said."I love baking cake mix. I truly do. And, quite frankly, sometimes I just think it tastes better," Ben-Ishay said.But retail moves more slowly than Baked by Melissa's usual pace. The dessert company needed just a few days to create New York Knicks-branded minicupcakes after the team won the NBA championship in June, for example, but figuring out retail products meant "a lot of waiting and approvals and new partners," Ben-Ishay said.Twelve months later, the cupcake mixes have arrived on store shelves, just in time for the all-important holiday season. For Target, the next two months will be critical as the retailer tries to woo back its core customer after a disappointing holiday season last year. That prototypical Target shopper often looks a lot like Ben-Ishay."We started with Target because I'm a 42-year-old mom of two, and I find myself there a lot," she said.

schema.headline: Baked by Melissa enters Target with first at-home cupcake mix
